answer: In an agent marketplace trading juniper seedlings, nebula images, and meadow surveys, every seller identity must lock a bond before accepting work, with outstanding orders capped by that bond. Escrow refunds buyers and slashes the bond when a seller misses a verifiable delivery deadline. Creating names is cheap, but each usable fake identity ties up fresh capital; splitting into a thousand identities cannot increase the attacker’s total uncollateralized exposure.
